why_ai: Pipeline infrastructure is not replaced by AI, and AI-written code raises build volume; operation is routine.
why_clarity: Every run records pass, fail, duration and cost against the change that triggered it.
why_digital: Code in, builds and deployments out, bought online from remote vendors.

why_ai: Most pipeline failures fall into a few recognisable classes an agent can diagnose from logs.
why_clarity: Recurring failure classes with logs that confirm whether the fix made the pipeline pass.
why_digital: Failures arrive as logs in chat channels and are resolved in code.

why_ai: Every build minute is already tied to a job, step and change; attribution is computation.
why_clarity: Spend is metered per job and step, so attribution reconciles exactly to the invoice.
why_digital: Usage records in, cost dashboards out, sold to platform and finance teams online.

why_ai: Rollback decisions on health signals are rule-based, though novel production incidents still need engineers.
why_clarity: Health signals give a fast, objective verdict on whether a release degraded users.
why_digital: Releases, telemetry and rollback decisions all happen in software.

why_ai: Tests run on physical boards and benches, so device orchestration resists pure software automation.
why_clarity: Tests pass or fail on hardware, but each device rig is set up differently.
why_digital: Firmware is digital but test targets are physical boards on lab benches.

why_ai: Every execution is recorded and joined to the change, so flake detection is statistical automation.
why_clarity: Flakiness is statistical, so confirming a test is truly flaky needs many reruns.
why_digital: Test execution history in, quarantine and signal reports out, all in the pipeline.

why_ai: Commodity compute compared on a spreadsheet; demand persists but any provider will do.
why_clarity: Queue time and cost per change are exact, instantly measured numbers.
why_digital: Hosted runners are bought, configured and switched entirely online.

why_ai: Build compute remains needed in 2031, but scheduling, caching and placement are routine and optimisable.
why_clarity: Each pipeline run has a measurable duration, cost and outcome.
why_digital: Pipelines execute as software on remote compute bought online.

why_ai: Code-boundary rules, special hardware and compliance evidence keep enterprises paying for controlled installs.
why_clarity: Builds pass or fail objectively, but each enterprise install is customised and old.
why_digital: Software installed inside the customer boundary, sold through enterprise sales cycles.

why_ai: Complete evidence sits in execution history, so impact analysis is a pure model problem.
why_clarity: Missed failures show up on the full run, giving objective feedback on selection.
why_digital: Execution history in, selected test sets out, inside the pipeline.

why_ai: Test ordering, early failure and local feedback are straightforward software optimisations.
why_clarity: Push-to-result interval is a measurable number paid every push by every developer.
why_digital: Developer feedback loops live entirely in code tools and pipelines.
